title: A Stretchable Nanowire UV-Vis-NIR Photodetector with High Performance

lanes.label: Classical tools
lanes.sub: collapsed to one node per state

states.title: Hypothesis and design
states.head: Wearable optoelectronics need a photodetector that covers UV to NIR and keeps working under large stretching. A PbS QD-P3HT hybrid nanowire written as a free-standing arch should sense UV to NIR and tolerate stretching.
states.detail: Absorbed: a1 (HYP/need), a2 (HYP/hypothesis), a3 (DES/base_system), a4 (DES/modification), a5 (DES/architecture), a6 (DES/route), a7 (DES/variable_sweep), a8 (PRC/synthesis), a9 (PRC/forming). Premises: PbS quantum dots act as NIR sensitisers in hybrid polymer photodetectors

states.title: Structure state
states.head: PbS QDs are dispersed through the body of the written P3HT nanowire. The written wire stands as a free arch spanning the electrode gap rather than lying on the substrate

states.title: Property state and mechanisms
states.head: The ON/OFF ratio rises with QD loading and falls with QD size, peaking at 60 wt% of 4.4 nm QDs. The hybrid wire responds from 365 to 940 nm, whereas the NIR response is absent without QDs.
states.detail: Absorbed: a12 (PRP/value), a13 (PRP/value), a14 (MEC/pathway), a15 (PRP/value), a17 (MEC/pathway). Premises: Photoinduced charge transfer between P3HT and PbS quantum dots quenches the QD photoluminescence; A larger PbS dot gives an unfavourable band offset that restricts hole transfer to P3HT; An arched free-standing wire accommodates substrate strain by geometric relaxation

states.title: Performance state
states.head: The 3x3 array holds its ON/OFF ratio and response time through stretching to 100% and 100 stretch cycles

states.title: Conclusion
states.head: Directly written PbS QD-P3HT nanowire arches give a stretchable UV-vis-NIR photodetector array with high and stable ON/OFF ratios

10.1002/adma.201404945#F1a.definition: Scheme of direct writing of a hybrid NW arch by the meniscus-guided approach. Inset: SEM image of a single hybrid NW arch on an Au–Al electrode
use: Using the blend solution, PbS QD-P3HT hybrid NWs were produced by a direct-writing technology, called the meniscus-guiding method.[17] Figure 1a schematically illustrates the direct writing of a hybrid NW arch.

10.1002/adma.201404945#F1b.definition: TEM image of a hybrid NW onto a carbon mesh on a copper grid. Inset: EDS spectrum of the hybrid NW
use: PbS QDs were uniformly dispersed in single hybrid NWs, as demonstrated by the TEM image of a single NW (Figure 1b).
The energy-dispersive X-ray spectroscopy (EDS) image of the NW (inset of Figure 1b) clearly indicates the presence of Pb and S elements originating from the PbS QDs.

The photoresponse of our single hybrid NWPDs, produced by directly integrating single $60\%$ PbS QD $(4.4\mathrm{nm}$ )-P3HT QD hybrid NW arches $r\approx250$ nm and $l\approx50~{\upmu\mathrm{m}}$ ) on Au–Al electrodes (inset of Figure 2a), was characterized using a broad spectral range from the UV to the NIR, as demonstrated in Figure 2.

First of all, the hybrid NWPDs showed a broad spectral photoresponse from the UV– vis to NIR (Figure 2a-c) range, which is related to the PbS QDs, as they act as NIR sensitizers.[ll Moreover, the photoresponse of P3HT NWPDs was limited to the UV–vis range (Figure S4, Supporting Information).

The photoresponse (from 365 to $940\mathrm{nm}$ of single hybrid NWPDs was significantly affected by the QD concentration, as demonstrated in Figure 3a and Figure S6 in the Supporting Information.
The ON/OFF ratios, obtained for our PbS QD $(4.4~\mathrm{nm})$ -P3HT hybrid NWPDs, largely increased with QD concentration for all wavelengths (Figure 3a).

use: The ON/OFF ratios, obtained for 60 wt% PbS QD-P3HT hybrid NWPDs, increased with decreasing QD size for all wavelengths tested, as shown in Figure 3b.

It is well known that the fraction of photoexcited excitons that are fuorescent, as probed by PL quenching, is significantly larger in PbS QDs (ca. $20\%$ [16] than in P3HT (ca. $1\%\%$ .1221 This indicates that the hole transfer from the QDs to P3HT contributes dominantly to the photoresponse of the hybrid NWPDs, which explains the increase of the ON/ OFF ratio with decreasing QD size (Figure 3b).

10.1002/adma.201404945#F3c.definition: UV– vis-NIR absorption spectra of PbS QD-P3HT hybrid flms on quartz substrates. (Inset: NIR absorption range)
use: This increase can be explained by the progressive enhancement in absorbance with QD concentration, as seen in the UV–vis–NIR absorption spectra for PbS QD $(4.4\mathrm{nm})$ )- P3HT hybrid flms deposited on quartz substrates (Figure 3c).

It should be noted that all of the hybrid films except the P3HT film (short dashed line) show absorption features at a wavelength of about $1150~\mathrm{nm}$ (inset of Figure 3c), which matches well with the absorption peak of the $4.4~\mathrm{nm}$ QDs (Figure S7, Supporting Information).

10.1002/adma.201404945#F3d.definition: PL spectra of the QDs (dashed lines) and blend (solid lines) solutions in the QD emission ranges for various QD sizes
use: This increase can be explained by photoluminescence (PL) quenching due to photoinduced charge transfer between P3HT and the PbS QDs.[12] We characterized the PL spectra of the blend (solid lines) solutions in the QD emission ranges for various QD sizes (Figure 3d).
The PL intensities in the blend solutions were quenched relative to those of the pristine QD solutions (dashed lines in Figure 3d).
